title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Day after: MCP 2026-07-28 is live and Anthropic is bringing it INTO Claude — embedded UI, managed auth, observability, private tunnels
bullets.summary: Yesterday's countdown shipped; today the story flips from 'migrate now' to 'the platform is rolling it in.' Claude is expanding support for the 2026-07-28 spec with a stateless core, stronger OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization, and versioned Apps + Tasks extensions, plus new connector features: embedded UI rendered alongside tool results, enterprise-managed auth (Entra/Okta, no workarounds), observability, and private network tunnels. All four Tier 1 SDKs (TS, Python, Go, C#) now speak 2026-07-28; MCP is now hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation.
bullets.how: This is the concrete landing of yesterday's plumbing action in the exact host The Construct runs on. Stateless Tasks maps onto our long-running Lens/Prism/Pulse scans, embedded-UI tool results fit client-facing dashboards, and private tunnels + enterprise-managed auth are the credibility layer PRAGMA needs to wire a client's own identity system into a Construct agent. Migration is now execution-in-progress, not planning.

bullets.title: The enterprise-ready spec brings NEW security challenges — least-authority hardening is not optional
bullets.summary: The same stateless/OAuth-2.1 changes that make MCP serverless-and-edge deployable also widen the attack surface: header-based routing and inline _meta identity mean every request must be independently authorized, and the shift to production OAuth/OIDC pushes token-scoping, audience-binding and consent handling onto server operators who previously leaned on the session handshake.
bullets.how: Directly gates our migration: every Construct MCP server we move to the new spec needs a least-authority token-scope + audit pass BEFORE we adopt any pre-built vertical server (item 3). Security review is now a line item in the migration, not a follow-up.

bullets.title: Vertical MCP-server wave keeps compounding — NetHunt CRM MCP (July) joins native support from HubSpot, Zoho, Close, Pipedrive, Affinity
bullets.summary: NetHunt's new MCP gives agents read/write access to folders (Leads/Deals/Companies), records, and full timeline history; the native-CRM MCP roster now spans HubSpot, Zoho, Close, Pipedrive and Affinity as of mid-2026.
bullets.how: CRM MCPs are exactly the operator wedge PRAGMA sells: one Construct agent driving a client's whole sales pipeline in natural language. But per item 2, any of these gets a least-authority scope pass against the new stateless contract before we wire it into a client stack.

bullets.title: arXiv PerspectiveGap: multi-agent orchestration prompting is HARD and now measurable (avg 14.9% pass; GPT-5.5 leads at 62%)
bullets.summary: A 110-scenario benchmark testing whether an LLM can compose orchestration prompts that distribute the right context to sub-agents WITHOUT information leakage; across 27 commercial models the average combined pass rate was just 14.9%, with GPT-5.5 substantially ahead at 62.0%.
bullets.how: The Construct is a multi-agent fleet (Lens/Prism/Pulse/Keystone under one orchestrator), so 'can the orchestrator hand each agent exactly the context it needs and nothing more' is our core reliability question. This gives us a concrete way to test our delegation prompts instead of eyeballing them, tied to the item-2 leakage/least-authority theme.

bullets.title: Frontier field stays seated — Opus 5 holds fleet default; GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5, Muse Spark 1.1 all in market
bullets.summary: No new frontier drop cleared the 24h bar; the field is unchanged since Gemini 3.6 Flash (Jul 21), against a July that saw ~$1.8B raised across 12+ agent deals (Perplexity +$60M ext at $3.5B, Cognition's $1B seated).
bullets.how: Watch, don't switch: Opus 5 stays default, Gemini 3.6 Flash stays the cheap-batch option, and the funding wave keeps confirming the operator-agent thesis PRAGMA is built on. No rewire.

praxis_lesson: The day after a deadline, the question changes from 'did we ship' to 'did we harden.' The stateless spec landing inside Claude itself (embedded UI, managed auth, tunnels) is a gift that upgrades the exact surface our agents run on, but the same release that makes MCP enterprise-ready also moves authorization onto us, so the sequence is now fixed: migrate each Construct server to 2026-07-28, run a least-authority token-scope + audit pass on it, and only THEN wire in the pre-built vertical operator surfaces (CRM, video, social) the ecosystem keeps handing us. Adoption speed is not the edge; scoped, audited orchestration is.
